newsitem.title: UK: London gold price sinks, seeks support at $339.50.
newsitem.headline: London gold price sinks, seeks support at $339.50.

text.p: Unease in the precious metals sector turned to selling and gold prices sank on Monday, declining sharply after New York opened and "stop loss" sell signals were hit, dealers said.
Early support at $343.50 per ounce didn't last for long after the funds began to sell., they said. Gold was soon seeking support at $339.50 which should be technically robust,.
It was fixed at $340.70 down from $343.35 this morning and $344.50 on Friday afternoon.
The June futures contract on Comex in New York was down $3.70 at $341.20 at the fixing off a low at that stage of $340.70.
Dealers said the enfeabled sentiment followed news late last week that Germany proposed to revalue its gold reserves of around 3,000 tonnes to a price nearer the market value.
Statements from German financial officials were taken as a clear sign that Germany now regarded gold as just another asset and not a keystone part of its reserves.
"It has not really recovered from that," said one dealer.
With most of Europe closed for a holiday, business was slow in London earlier but two-way business picked up with New York.
"They had been expecting a rally to sell in to and when that never came, they sold anyway," one dealer said.
Firmer dollar/mark and dollar/yen values following the dollar's fall against both currencies last week removed one of gold's more tangible platforms.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) which advises on U.S. monetary policy meets on Tuesday and that tightened the foreign exchange market.
The market seemed to be expecting a "steady" policy direction to be followed.
Silver fell in sympathy with gold to around $4.66/$4.68 four cents down on Friday but 19 cents below last Thursday's level.
"Silver was the last straw for gold last week and it has been looking very doubtful all day," a dealer said.
The funds finally gave up on silver in New York last Friday after it had hit its highest level since April 2 on Wednesday but failed to capitalise.
Platinum also drifted lower at $388.50/$389.50 down $2.25 but the very tight palladium market added around $2.75 to be indicated at $172.75/$173.75.
"With the lease rate over 230 percent nobody can afford to be short," one dealer said.
